walkthroughs.body_html:
Fundamentals Of Algorithms — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Fundamentals Of Algorithms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Fundamentals Of Algorithms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique involves breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems?
options: Abstraction
Decomposition
Iteration
Encapsulation

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a trace table?
options: To compile code
To track variable values during execution
To draw a flowchart
To store program output

mcqs.q: What is the worst-case complexity of bubble sort?
options: O(n) because it just passes through the list.
O(n squared).
O(1) - because it is fast.
O(log n).

mcqs.q: What is the time complexity of binary search?
options: IP is for input, MAC is for output.
O(log n).
O(n) - because it searches through items.
O(1) - because it is fast.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between an IP address and a MAC address?
options: MAC is a hardware identifier (fixed); IP is a logical network address (assignable).
IP is for input, MAC is for output.
They are the same thing with different names.
O(log n).
